region: DataFeel Dot contact surface — activity-associated profile

loci.basis: NTC thermistor at contact surface. Mild warmth (36–40 °C) is associated with increased local metabolic activity and vasodilation. Thermoelectric element provides bidirectional control.

Normalised time-of-day (0.0 = midnight, 1.0 = midnight). Activity phase approximately 0.25–0.75 (06:00–18:00 local). Host-supplied; not measured by the device. Used to select circadian-appropriate optical output.

170 Hz resonant actuator. Pacinian corpuscles are most sensitive in the 200–300 Hz range; 170 Hz is within the activation window. Vibrotactile stimulation at moderate amplitude activates large-diameter Aβ afferents, consistent with gate-control analgesic pathways. Activity profile uses higher amplitude range.

RGB blue channel, ~466 nm. Intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs) expressing melanopsin have peak sensitivity near 480 nm; 466 nm is within the activation range. Blue-enriched illumination during the active phase is associated with circadian synchronisation and suppression of melatonin secretion (Brainard et al., 2001; Thapan et al., 2001). This association is retinal and systemic, not a local tissue effect of the Dot LED.

relations.description: Thermal disturbance (Δ) drives haptic amplitude via accumulated sigma. A detected temperature change at the contact surface produces a coordinated vibrotactile response.

Circadian phase drives blue channel intensity. During the activity phase (higher time_of_day_phase value), blue output is proportional to the phase value, consistent with the role of blue-enriched light in daytime circadian entrainment.

provenance: Robin Macomber, Metatron Dynamics, Inc. — 2026-10-21. V0.2 activity-associated profile. Scientific basis in docs/verification_record.md.
